sections.heading: Topic 1: Number & Algebra (Sequences, Logs & Binomial) Practice Exercises

questions.q: Consider the function \( f(x) = 2x + 5 \). What is the value of \( f(3) \)?
questions.answer: To find \( f(3) \), substitute \( x=3 \) into the function \( f(x) = 2x + 5 \). \( f(3) = 2(3) + 5 = 6 + 5 = 11 \). [M1] [A1]

questions.q: The graph of the quadratic function \( f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 5 \) is shown below. Find the value of the y-intercept.
questions.answer: The y-intercept of a function occurs where the graph crosses the y-axis, which is when \( x = 0 \). For the function \( f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 5 \), when \( x = 0 \), we have \( f(0) = (0)^2 - 6(0) + 5 = 0 - 0 + 5 = 5 \). Therefore, the y-intercept is 5. [M1] [A1]

questions.q: Consider the function \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 \) and the line \( g(x) = x - 1 \). The graph of these functions is shown below. Find the coordinates of the point where the line intersects the parabola.
questions.answer: To find the intersection points, we set the two functions equal to each other: \( f(x) = g(x) \) \( x^2 - 4x + 3 = x - 1 \) \( x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0 \) Factoring the quadratic equation: \( (x-1)(x-4) = 0 \) This gives us two possible x-values for the intersection points: \( x=1 \) or \( x=4 \). Using \( g(x) = x-1 \) to find the corresponding y-values: For \( x=1 \): \( y = 1 - 1 = 0 \). The intersection point is \( (1, 0) \). For \( x=4 \): \( y = 4 - 1 = 3 \). The intersection point is \( (4, 3) \). Looking at the graph, one of the intersection points is \( (1, 0) \). [M1] [A1]
Any nonzero number to power 0 is 1. [M1] [A1]

questions.q: The graph of the quadratic function \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \) is shown below. It passes through the points \( (0, -3) \), \( (1, 0) \), and \( (-1, -4) \). Find the value of \( c \).
questions.answer: The general form of a quadratic function is \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \). The graph of the function passes through the point \( (0, -3) \). Substituting these coordinates into the function, we get: \( f(0) = a(0)^2 + b(0) + c \). Since \( f(0) = -3 \), we have \( -3 = 0 + 0 + c \), which means \( c = -3 \). [M1] [A1]

questions.q: Consider the function \( f(x) = 2x - 3 \). Determine the value of \( f(3) \).
questions.answer: To find the value of \( f(3) \), substitute \( x=3 \) into the function \( f(x) = 2x - 3 \). \( f(3) = 2(3) - 3 \) \( f(3) = 6 - 3 \) \( f(3) = 3 \) [M1] [A1]
Working through this algebra step: \( 3^x=9=(3)^{2} \Rightarrow x=2 \). [M1] [A1]
